messages:
anya (PM): quick sync — I'm drafting the PRD for launch gates around audit logs + key management. Need to lock scope for acceptance criteria so engineering can estimate. TL;DR: customers are asking for longer retention, per-customer KMS keys (HSM-backed), and an export path for compliance.

sam (Security Eng): echo. important to separate internal telemetry from compliance-grade audit trails. propose two tiers: "core-audit" (immutable, tamper-evident) and "app-telemetry" (aggregated, sampled).

ravi (Eng Lead): FYI: runtime can emit both streams; main cost is storage + egress for exports. need clear retention defaults and opt-in flags before we size infra.

maria (Compliance): for SOC2/ISO scope: auditors expect 12 months minimum accessible logs, plus archive for legal hold. some regulated customers (finance/health) will request 3–7 years. we should include a configurable retention policy per org with enforcement and an approved default.

kevin (Solutions): customers asking: "can we have our own KMS key and the ability to pull an end-to-end chain of custody for a given request?" They want exportable packages for audits.

anya (PM): proposed PRD items (high level):
- Acceptance criteria:
  1) Audit trail contains immutable records for every inference request (request_id, model_id, model_version, timestamps, auth_principal, token counts, status).
  2) Raw prompt and response stored only if customer enables "retain-payloads"; otherwise store salted hash of prompt + redacted metadata.
  3) Per-org KMS support: allow customer-supplied key (bring-your-key) backed by HSM; fallback to Redwood-managed KMS if not configured.
  4) Export: ability to generate a signed, time-bounded export bundle (logs + key chain) within 24 hours.
  5) Retention policy UI/API: default 12 months, configurable to 7 years max for enterprise, with legal hold toggle.
  6) Tamper evidence: logs immutability via append-only storage + periodic checksums (sha256) and an audit ledger.

sam (Security Eng): additions / edge cases: 
- HSM availability: plan for key-rotation windows and HSM outage fallback. must define behavior when customer-owned KMS is unreachable (fail closed vs fail open). my recommendation: fail closed for operations requiring key (decrypting stored payloads), but allow read-only exports of redacted metadata.
- Key rotation: support key rotation without losing ability to verify older logs (i.e., wrap old keys with new KMS key or store key versions in chain-of-trust).
- Replay risk: don't log full PII in cleartext to core-audit unless customer explicitly consents.

liz (Legal): GDPR note — right-to-be-forgotten requests create tension with immutable audit trails. recommended approach: keep immutable audit indices (hashes, metadata) and delete / purge raw payloads on request. records that must be retained for legal hold should be flagged and routed through compliance for exceptions. document this in PRD as "deletion mechanics and exception flow".

maria (Compliance): also call out: SOC2 auditors expect access controls around who can run exports and view raw payloads. include RBAC acceptance criteria and an export audit (who, when, why).

kevin (Solutions): sample export format request from customers — zipped JSONL + signatures. include sample config in PRD so we can prototype: 
```json
{
  "export_version": "1.0",
  "org_id": "acct_123",
  "time_range": ["2025-01-01T00:00:00Z","2025-01-31T23:59:59Z"],
  "files": ["audit-core.jsonl","payloads.enc"],
  "signature": "BASE64SIG"
}
```

anya (PM): edge cases we need to enumerate in RFC: 
- partial writes during region failover,
- cross-region replication delays affecting immutability guarantees,
- export when KMS is customer-managed and the key is revoked,
- how we surface retention/expiry to customers (API+console).

ravi (Eng Lead): for partial writes: we can write with a two-phase commit to object store plus ledger entry. costy but feasible for compliance-tier orgs only. need to mark this as an optional "strong-consistency" toggle in PRD.

sam (Security Eng): KMS revocation: export should fail if key is revoked and payloads are encrypted and not recoverable. we should surface a clear error and a remediation path (customer must provide recovery key or allow Redwood to re-encrypt with a fallback key under legal process). document expected SLAs for export attempts.

maria (Compliance): Acceptance test cases suggestion: 
- create org with default policy, generate 10k requests, verify retention purge after X days, verify legal hold prevents purge, verify export package integrity and signature validation.
- attempt right-to-be-forgotten for user_id that appears in payloads; verify raw payloads removed but audit index (hash) remains with provenance info.

anya (PM): decision needed from legal/security on fail-closed vs fail-open for KMS outages. also need sign-off on retention defaults (12 months default, 36 months enterprise optional).

liz (Legal): lean conservative: default 12 months. fail-closed for operations that would expose protected data. provide a documented escalation path for customers who require different behavior.

sam (Security Eng): +1 fail-closed for decryption. provide a "read-only redacted" fallback that returns metadata and hashes.

anya (PM): next steps / action items: 
- sam: write security appendix for RFC (key rotation, outage behavior, ledger design) — due EOD Friday.
- r avi: prototype two-tier logging pipeline & estimate infra cost — due next Wed.
- maria: draft SOC2/ISO acceptance matrix and test cases — due next Tue.
- liz: short legal doc on GDPR interplay + recommended exception flow — due next Thu.
- kevin: collect sample customer export requirements and sample S3/transfer patterns — ongoing.

audit-bot: created rfc/2026-audit-retention-playbook (link: http://rfd.internal/rfc-2026-audit-retention-playbook)

anya (PM): ok thanks all — I'll fold these into the PRD draft and ping reviewers once I have the first pass. :thumbsup:
